EIBUN.name: EIBUN
EIBUN.desc: Provisional #1 among the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten my way through (14/15). A famous shop featured on Horiemon's “Adult Playground” map. The No.1 most popular “BUNBUN soba” is a luxurious bowl topped with four kinds of meat.
t: It was featured in the “Horiemon 'Adult Playground' Nationwide Map” (paid), and after watching it I went to eat there right away in July 2022 lol

I've still only been to a fraction of the Okinawa soba shops on the main island of Okinawa, nowhere near conquering them all, but I think this is the most delicious Okinawa soba I've had so far. As expected of a recommendation from the gourmet Mr. Horie ☺

I'd heard there would be a line, so after enjoying my hobby of surfing first thing in the morning at the Suicide Cliff point in Itoman City, I arrived around 10 o'clock even though the opening time was 11 ☺ Naturally, at that hour I was easily the first one there.
However, there was a reception list placed at the shop entrance, and some people wrote down a reservation and then left the shop for a while, so I hurriedly put my name on the reception list too.
Right before the 11 o'clock opening time, customers started lining up. As expected, there are a lot of tourists. *The shop has no parking lot. There is coin parking in front of the shop.
The “EIBUN” entrance. The design is stylish, isn't it

This is the situation when I finished eating and left the shop: from just before the 11 o'clock opening, the number of customers suddenly increased. I think there's probably a line continuously until closing. It's better to put your name on the reception list early and eat early.
When I went inside, “BUNBUN soba,” whose name resembles the shop's name, was being recommended as the No.1 most popular, so I ordered it.
Recommended menu

First, a sip of the soup. The bonito-based broth really comes through and it's delicious. The moment I drank it, it was a deliciousness no shop before had. The noodles are thin and straight. There are four toppings (braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), makanai meat, soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), and seared soft-bone pork ribs), and all of them are well-seasoned and the best lol. I thought the balance of soup, noodles, and toppings was the best of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at so far.
“BUNBUN soba” (¥1,000), recommended as the No.1 most popular

Rating (14/15): Wow, it seems the owner is from mainland Japan, and the shop's name seems to come from his own name; apparently he opened the shop after training at a famous Okinawa soba shop. I'm looking forward to seeing whether an Okinawa soba shop will ever come along that I think surpasses this deliciousness.

STAND EIBUN.name: STAND EIBUN
STAND EIBUN.desc: The second shop of provisional #1 “EIBUN” (14/15). The most popular item is the sea lettuce (āsa) soba. A hidden gem where you can enjoy a bowl of the same level without standing in the main shop's line.
t: “EIBUN” is the shop I think is the most delicious of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at so far, but I recently found out they opened a second shop around April 2023(?), so I went to eat there in February 2024 😁
STAND EIBUN (a stylish exterior that doesn't lose to the main shop 😆)
This second shop was really close to the main shop (^0^;)

On top of that, it was two doors down from “Okinawa Pork Soba,” which I visited the other day as the 6th of 34 shops in the 13th stamp rally (^0^;)　As usual, I go with no research and just wing it, so I didn't know (^0^;)

What surprised me even more is that on this day too the main shop had its usual line and didn't feel easy to drop into, but the second shop had no line in particular. When I stood in front of the entrance, a staff member guided me in, saying “Please, come in.”
The number of customers is completely different between the main shop and the second shop.

When I went inside, there was a meal ticket machine installed, so I ordered from the menu. I believe the main shop accepted cashless payment, but unfortunately this one seems to be cash only. The meal ticket machine is a new type too, so I hope they'll support cashless payment in the future.

In the staff member's explanation of the menu in front of the meal ticket machine, they said something like “the sea lettuce (āsa) soba is the most popular,” so this time I decided to order the “sea lettuce (āsa) soba” 😁
I was shown to a counter seat, and while I waited I looked around the stylish interior 😄
Drinks are self-service.
The condiment containers placed on the table are stylish too
Besides the usual “kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori),” there was also something called “gōmāgūsu.” That's new.
The regular “kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori).” As expected, the container has a stylish look 😆
There are various other condiments too 😄
T-shirts, roasted green tea (hojicha), bowls, and so on are sold inside the shop. Stylish 😄
While I was observing the interior, the “sea lettuce (āsa) soba” arrived. It looks delicious 😋
Sea lettuce (āsa) soba　¥1,080
The blue bowl is the same as at the main shop “EIBUN” 😄　I was about to taste the soup right away, but there were no chopsticks?
There were no chopsticks on the table, and thinking “Huh? Did the staff forget?”, I asked whether there were chopsticks, and the answer was “They're in the drawer” (°°)
Chopsticks, wet towels, and condiments were in the drawer (^0^;)　I didn't notice (^0^;)
When I checked the drawer, they were inside. Looking closely, there was a label-maker sticker in small letters on the counter wall saying that chopsticks and wet towels are in the drawer (^0^;)
I didn't notice (^0^;)　Starting over, I took a sip of the soup. It's a soup with the bonito broth coming through, and I thought, as expected, EIBUN is delicious.

Next, when I tasted the soup together with the sea lettuce (āsa), I could also feel the flavor of the seashore, and this was delicious too 😋　According to what I googled, before opening EIBUN the manager also trained at “Nakamura Soba” in Onna Village, and it reminded me of Nakamura Soba's sea lettuce (āsa) soba too 😆
Sea lettuce (āsa) soba　¥1,080

Next, I have the noodles. The medium-thick fresh noodles have a chewy, springy feel, and they're delicious too 😄　The toppings, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), still had a bit of sinewy texture, but they're tender and delicious. Moreover, unlike other shops, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were finished with a fairly sweet flavor, rich and deep, and I found these delicious too.

Then, in the second half, I changed up the flavor of the soup with the “gōmāgūsu.” I could feel the nice aroma of sesame oil and the sourness of vinegar too, and it became a new soup. It goes well with it, and I thought this was delicious too 😄

Rating (14/15): Although it's the second shop, I had EIBUN's Okinawa soba for the first time in a while, and as expected I thought it was high-level and delicious. Looking at “noodles,” “soup,” and “toppings” individually, there are other shops that are just as delicious, but I think what's amazing about EIBUN is that the noodles, soup, and toppings are all in balance. Moreover, while the main shop has a line, this one maybe isn't well-known yet, so you can eat the same taste without getting caught in a line, which makes it recommended 😆　Also, it would be even better if they supported cashless payment soon 👍

木灰そば とらや.name: Mokkai Soba Toraya
木灰そば とらや.desc: A famous mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye) shop in Akamine near Naha Airport. Clear soup with plenty of bonito broth, and house-made noodles you can choose from medium-thin or flat. The melt-apart bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) served on a separate plate are superb.
t: This article was written with AI (Chat GPT 4o) and partially edited by me 😁

I ate here in September 2024 😄　I went to “Mokkai Soba Toraya” in Akamine, Naha City, and was amazed at how delicious its Okinawa soba was ✨. From the atmosphere of the shop to the soba served, the overall quality is very high, and as an Okinawa soba lover it's a shop I really want to recommend to everyone, so it's listed in my “Okinawa soba shops that hold their own against my recommended shops” corner 😆
Mokkai Soba Toraya

When you enter the shop, the first thing that catches your eye is the ticket machine. There's a wide variety on the menu, such as Okinawa soba, bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, and set menus with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) (rice cooked with ingredients), and everything makes you want to eat it. I chose the “bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba” without hesitation, but next time I'd like to try the other menu items too 🍚.
You can choose the noodles from medium-thin or flat noodles, and I decided to go with the recommended “medium-thin noodles.”
The meal ticket machine installed near the shop entrance
The noodles are the choosable type

After ordering, while I waited I looked around the shop, and a warm space with a wood-based design spread out before me. Okinawan-style decorations line the walls, and pickled red ginger and glass cups are neatly arranged on the counter, giving the impression that attention has been paid to every detail. It's mainly counter seats, which makes it easy to go in even alone, a nice point too 😊.
The counter inside the shop
Bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, medium　¥850

After a while, the “bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba” was served. The clear soup, the medium-thin noodles, and the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) served on a separate plate are striking. First, a sip of the soup. The bonito broth really comes through, and the rich aroma that spreads softly in your mouth is irresistible 😋.
Bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, medium　¥850

Next, I had the noodles. These are house-made noodles, and this time I chose the recommended medium-thin noodles. They're springy yet slide down smoothly, a very pleasant texture. They go perfectly with the soup too, and my chopsticks kept moving. When you hear “mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye),” you expect a unique flavor, but this time I didn't really notice that flavor. However, the noodles were boiled just right, and the quality was delicious enough as is 🍜.

And the main event, the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki)! These are served on a separate plate. I appreciate this consideration. It's a trick to avoid spoiling the taste of the soup, so you can enjoy the flavor of the bonito broth to the very end. The bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) are surprisingly tender, so tender they fall apart in your mouth. The sauce has soaked in thoroughly, and this alone is a very satisfying dish. Being able to enjoy them in a way only possible with separate-plate service is also one of the features of “Mokkai Soba Toraya.”

Overall, the Okinawa soba here comes together at a very high level. It's a shop I'd love for people who like bonito broth to try! Also, the atmosphere inside is comfortable, and you can drop in casually even alone. Next time I'd like to try the set with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) and other menu items ✨.
Please be sure to fully enjoy the charm of Okinawa soba at “Mokkai Soba Toraya”! I'm sure you'll be satisfied 😊.

Rating (12/15): I thought it was a high-level Okinawa soba shop with a good balance of noodles, soup, and toppings. It's close to the airport too, so how about trying it at least once, both tourists and locals? It's recommended 😄

宮古そば みやらび.name: Miyako Soba Miyarabi
宮古そば みやらび.desc: A Miyako soba specialty shop with a reddish-brown triangular roof, 10 minutes by car from Naha Airport. A bowl with a gentle pork-bone-based soup, thin straight noodles with a round cross-section, and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and lean pork on top. The interior has a Showa-retro feel, and turnover is quick.
t: This article was written with AI (Chat GPT o3) and partially edited by me 😁
I went to eat here in December 2024 😄

About 10 minutes by car from Naha Airport, a reddish-brown triangular roof appears all on its own in a corner of Gushi. That's “Miyako Soba Miyarabi” 🚗💨. A well-worn “Open” sign hangs from the wooden pillar at the entrance, and the purple flag proudly shows the words “Miyako Soba” in white. It makes your heart race.
Miyako Soba　Miyarabi
The meal ticket machine installed at the shop entrance

Right when you open the door, there's the meal ticket machine. More than 50 buttons, big and small, are lined up, and handwritten notes like “10-yen coins cannot be used” and “Lunch service” announcements are pasted all over it. Basic soba starts from around ¥700, and I'm surprised by the breadth of the lineup, which includes sets, soups, and even champuru (Okinawan stir-fry) 😲. This time I pushed the button without hesitation for the signature menu item that's even in the shop's name, “Miyako soba (¥750).” As soon as I put the meal ticket on the counter, cooking began briskly in the kitchen in the back.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

The wall side of the L-shaped counter inside has flower-patterned, mosaic-style glass, a bit like a Showa-retro coffee shop. At lunchtime it's sure to be full, but turnover is quick, and from handing over the meal ticket until the bowl arrives felt like about 5 minutes. A welcome speed for someone who wants to drop in quickly between sightseeing ⏱️.
Miyako soba　¥750

Now, the Miyako soba that appeared in front of me. The soup, clear yet slightly cloudy, has the gentle aroma of a pork bone base. It's not the “original Miyako style” where the toppings hide under the noodles; instead, the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and lean pork (loin) sit proudly on top. Pale green chopped green onions float on it, and although it looks simple, it's a bowl with a certain dignity.
First, a sip with the soup spoon. It's pork bone based.
Miyako soba　¥750
The noodles are thin and straight with a round cross-section, typical of Miyako soba. The firmness is modest, on the soft side 🍜.
The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) has a just-right balance of fat and lean, while the lean pork has a solid bite. Both have a sinewy texture 😆.

When I suddenly looked around, the place was bustling with customers. Even though it's located near the airport, it doesn't go all-in on tourist-spot prices; it's a shop that stays close to local daily life, and that atmosphere fills the shop, making it comfortable.

Rating (9/15): There's no standout flashiness, but it was a Miyako soba that embodies “just plain delicious” and stays close to everyday life. That's what I felt Miyarabi's Miyako soba is. It's a little away from central Naha City, but it's perfect for filling up before returning your rental car or for lunch on the way to the airport. How about trying it at least once ✨. 🥢

沖縄そば くいな.name: Okinawa Soba Kuina
沖縄そば くいな.desc: Produced by Horiemon, opened in April 2024. The signature dish is “Island Soba,” with a smooth combined broth of chicken, bonito, and pork bone and Nago-style flat noodles. A shop where the creative items like nbusa soba and inamuruchi mixed soba also catch your interest.
t: I ate here in April 2024 😄　This shop is produced by Horiemon and had just opened on April 26. Since it's run by the gourmet Mr. Horie, I came this time with high expectations 😁
Okinawa Soba　Kuina

When I went inside, a staff member explained the menu using a menu sheet. I forgot to take a photo of the menu sheet, but I decided to order the “Island Soba,” which was recommended with “for first-timers.” The other soba menu items are “Island Noodle (apparently with a blend of house-made seasonings),” “nbusa soba (Shirinkawa tofu + sea lettuce (āsa) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku)),” and “inamuruchi mixed soba,” so they've narrowed it down.
A flyer from Okinawa Soba Kuina
An explanation of the house-made seasonings posted on the wall (apparently you can taste them if you order the Island Noodle)
Island Soba　¥950

Here it is 😆　First, I taste the soup. It seems to be a combined broth of chicken, bonito, and pork bone, and it has a smooth feel with a slightly pronounced pork bone flavor. I think it's a taste other shops don't have.
Island Soba　¥950

Next, I have the noodles. They're fresh noodles, a flat type like the ones you see in Nago's Okinawa soba. I thought they were just plain delicious, but somehow I could feel hard cores remaining here and there. Maybe because they'd just opened and weren't used to it yet, I thought the boiling was uneven.
The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are melt-in-your-mouth tender too, but a sinewy texture remains.
Rating (9/15): This time, since it's a shop produced by the gourmet Horiemon, I had pretty high expectations, but it felt about “just plain delicious, I guess” (^0^;)

I think the noodle boiling was inconsistent too, so that's a shame. But I'd like to try their other creative Okinawa soba menu items. It's close to Kokusai-dori (near the prefectural office), so how about trying it once?

SHIKAKU.name: SHIKAKU
SHIKAKU.desc: A luxurious Okinawa soba shop on the 1st floor of the Southwest Grand Hotel. Its feature is the kettle (teapot) style where the noodles and soup come separately, and the dashi chazuke, made by pouring the kettle's broth over the tuna nakaochi rice, is also recommended.
t: This article was written with AI (Gemini Pro) and partially edited by me 😁
I went to eat here in February 2025 😄

This time I visited “SHIKAKU,” located on the 1st floor of the “Southwest Grand Hotel” in Kumoji, Naha City. The aura is different from the exterior alone. Since it's on the 1st floor of a hotel, there's a shisa sitting against a stylish exposed-concrete wall, and even this shisa looks somehow sleek, like modern art ✨
SHIKAKU is on the 1st floor of the Southwest Grand Hotel
SHIKAKU is on the 1st floor of the Southwest Grand Hotel
SHIKAKU is on the 1st floor of the Southwest Grand Hotel
SHIKAKU
SHIKAKU
SHIKAKU
Standing in front of the shop, a sense of luxury is in the air. But as an Okinawa soba lover, I summoned my courage and charged in!

When I went inside, the lighting was turned down quite low, and it had an atmosphere like a bar at dinnertime or an upscale teppanyaki restaurant. It's moody even though it's daytime, a space you could use for a date. And above all, what surprised me was the staff's service! When showing me to my seat, they actually pulled out my chair and escorted me, just like at a hotel restaurant…! Having my chair pulled out when I came to eat Okinawa soba may be a first in my life (lol). It makes you sit up a little straighter 😳
Inside the shop
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu

Now, when I sat down and opened the menu, it was another simple and stylish design. The “SHIKAKU soba” regular is ¥1,400 and the large is ¥1,600. I ordered the “SHIKAKU soba (regular)” and the side dish the staff recommended, “tuna nakaochi rice (¥700)” 🍜
After a while, this set was brought out.
SHIKAKU soba (regular) ¥1,400, tuna nakaochi rice　¥700

The style is unique! The bowl with the noodles and toppings and a silver kettle with the soup came out separately. This is the same style as the long-established “Yae Shokudo” in Nago City! I never thought I'd encounter this kettle style at a hotel in Naha. But it's not a homey kettle like Yae Shokudo's; it has the look of a sleek stainless-steel teapot, and I feel the stylishness here too ✨
This ritual of pouring the soup yourself from the kettle is exciting. Every time you pour, the nice aroma of bonito broth wafts up. The good thing about this style is that the soup stays piping hot.
First, I try a sip of the soup. Yeah, the bonito broth comes through.
SHIKAKU soba (regular) ¥1,400

Next, I have the noodles. The noodles are a thin type with a slight wave. When I slurp them, they have a smooth, slippery texture, and they're boiled fairly soft. As someone who likes noodles with strong firmness, I'd like a little more chewiness / bite 🤔

The toppings are braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and fish cake (kamaboko), plus green onions and bonito flakes. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is simmered tender, and the seasoning is neither too strong nor too light, just right. The bonito flakes sprinkled on top further bring out the aroma of the soup, and the flavor is really good 👍
Tuna nakaochi rice　¥700

And then the side dish, the “tuna nakaochi rice”! It comes with wasabi and looks delicious, but I poured the broth from the kettle holding the soba soup over the tuna rice and ate it like dashi chazuke.

This was exactly right! 🐟✨ The sweetness of the tuna's fat combines with the piping-hot bonito broth, and the half-rare tuna melts in your mouth. The wasabi adds an accent, and you can just shovel it down. I really want everyone to try it too!

Rating (9/15): My overall impression is that the taste is just plain delicious. However, there's no denying that it's “hotel pricing~.” With ¥1,400 for Okinawa soba, and over ¥2,000 with rice too, I think it's a shop for a sightseeing memory or for when you want a meal in a nice atmosphere, rather than an everyday lunch.

The atmosphere inside is supremely luxurious, and the staff's service is wonderful, so it has value as an “experience.” However, if it competes purely on “the taste of Okinawa soba,” compared with other shops, my honest feeling is that it ends up with a slightly harsher rating in terms of cost performance 😅
But the contrast of pouring the soup yourself from a kettle in this luxurious space was fun, and it's the perfect shop for a conversation topic! Thank you for the meal 🙏
